findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30 — Any accepted team member can install or replace a team OAuth integration because the team branch checks membership but never requires admin access.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The sync branch always returns a raw Fetch Response even though callers expect mutually incompatible SDK objects or provider-specific response bodies, breaking synced refreshes for Google, HubSpot, Lark, Teams, and Webex.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — The computed schema keys collapse to a literal object-string key, so Zod strips every expiry field and the helper persists a fabricated refresh token instead of the caller's token metadata.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — A synced refresh response has no data property, and the resulting exception is silently swallowed so the caller receives the expired Google client as if refresh succeeded.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101 — After successfully refreshing and persisting Salesforce tokens, the connection is still constructed with the stale pre-refresh access token and fails until a later reconstruction.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Secret verification fails open when CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset because a request with no matching header compares undefined equal to undefined.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73 — Updating a previously invalidated credential changes only its key and returns 200 while leaving invalid=true, so successful synchronization does not restore the integration.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — The find-then-create sequence is non-atomic, allowing concurrent first-delivery webhooks to create duplicate credentials or fail one delivery after external state has advanced.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:56 — Decrypted credential JSON is never validated against the selected app's credential schema, so an authenticated malformed delivery is acknowledged and corrupts the live credential.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The configured sync endpoint returns a Fetch Response, but this adapter reads the Axios-only `data` property so synced Google token refreshes are discarded.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — The shared sync helper returns a Fetch Response while this caller treats it as HubSpot's camelCase token object, persisting undefined tokens and an invalid expiry.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The advertised access-token-and-expiry response contract does not actually accept or preserve an arbitrary expiry field because the computed Zod key becomes a literal property and unknown fields are stripped.
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — With no configured webhook secret, an absent header compares as `undefined` and permits an unauthenticated credential write.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The computed Zod keys become `"[object Object]"`, so the stripping object schema drops real expiry and token fields from sync responses.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Credential-sync returns a Fetch `Response`, but this branch reads Axios-style `.data`, so synced Google refreshes throw before updating the token.
packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — This saves the `safeParse` result wrapper as the credential key rather than its `.data`, corrupting every refreshed Google credential.
packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Credential-sync returns a Fetch `Response`, but it is treated as a `HubspotToken`, causing undefined token fields to be persisted.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The `any` callback and inferred union return erase whether callers receive a Fetch `Response` or an SDK-specific token object, allowing every adapter to assume an incompatible shape without type checking.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — Accepting `any` and `ZodTypeAny` and returning the whole safe-parse wrapper leaks validation mechanics while discarding the schema's inferred token type, which has already led callers to consume and persist the result inconsistently.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Token validation is coupled to global environment state instead of the response source, so local refreshes that fall back because a credential has no userId are still parsed under the sync-endpoint contract.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:40 — Resolving the app through both the database and `appStoreMetadata` creates two registries that must remain synchronized for the webhook to accept an integration.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — The team lookup selects every member userId even though only the team's existence is used, leaving dead query shape and unnecessary coupling to member records.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — Every client construction unconditionally refreshes Salesforce tokens and writes the credential, adding a remote call and database write even while the access token is valid.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — The membership existence check selects every member userId for the team even though only the team id is used, causing unbounded materialization for large teams.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no abort timeout, so an unavailable sync service can indefinitely block expired-token booking requests.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Sync mode returns a Fetch Response but this path reads a Gaxios `.data` field, so every Google token refresh through the sync endpoint falls back to the expired token.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — Persisting the SafeParse result rather than its `.data` stores `{success,data}` as the Google credential and makes subsequent authentications fail validation.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Sync mode returns a Fetch Response where HubSpot expects a parsed token object, so refresh writes/uses undefined token fields and leaves the client unauthenticated.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 — The sync response is documented to omit refresh tokens, but the parser injects `"refresh_token"` and this merge overwrites the usable Office 365 refresh token.

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — Saving the access-token-only sync response replaces the Teams credential and drops its refresh token, preventing recovery when the next token expires.
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:32 — Accepted non-admin team members can create a team-wide OAuth credential because only membership is checked
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — An unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET makes an absent header compare equal to undefined and bypasses webhook authentication
packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — OAuth state is unauthenticated client JSON with no session-bound nonce, enabling OAuth credential-linking CSRF

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — No sync-enabled refresh test exercises a real Fetch Response, so the code reads the nonexistent res.data and silently keeps the expired token.
packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — No sync-enabled HubSpot test verifies the endpoint response is decoded before treating the Fetch Response itself as HubspotToken credentials.
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — No compile or service-construction test covers the new Salesforce refresh path, which references prisma without importing it.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — The new credential-writing webhook has no request-level tests covering authentication, malformed encrypted payloads, and both create and update behavior.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — The shared provider-routing helper has no tests for enabled, disabled, team-owned, non-2xx, or malformed-response branches despite changing refresh behavior across six integrations.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — A synced refresh response has no data property, and the resulting exception is silently swallowed so the caller receives the expired Google client as if refresh succeeded.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, the refreshAccessToken function now uses refreshOAuthTokens which can return either the result of myGoogleAuth.refreshToken() (which has a .res property with .data) or a fetch Response from the credential sync endpoint (which has no .data property). The code on line 94 does `const token = res?.data` - when using the sync endpoint, res is a fetch Response object which doesn't have a .data property, so token would be undefined. Then googleCredentials.access_token and expiry_date would be set to undefined. The try-catch block would catch any errors silently (the catch block just logs and returns myGoogleAuth), so the caller would receive the original expired credentials. This is a real bug where the synced refresh path doesn't properly extract the token data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — Secret verification fails open when CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset because a request with no matching header compares undefined equal to undefined.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the code in apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the secret verification compares `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret']` against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (undefined), and a request comes in without that header (also undefined), the comparison `undefined !== undefined` is false, so the check passes. However, the earlier check at line 17-19 checks `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` which according to packages/lib/constants.ts requires both CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY to be set. So if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset, APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED would be falsy and the function would return 403 at line 18 before reaching the secret comparison. The finding appears to be a hallucination because the earlier guard prevents the scenario described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73 — Updating a previously invalidated credential changes only its key and returns 200 while leaving invalid=true, so successful synchronization does not restore the integration.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the code at lines 68-78 shows that when updating an existing credential, only the 'key' field is updated via prisma.credential.update(). The Credential model likely has an 'invalid' field (common pattern for OAuth credentials that have been revoked/expired). If a credential was previously marked as invalid=true, this update operation would only change the key but leave invalid=true, meaning the credential would still appear invalid even after successful synchronization. This is a real bug - the update should also set invalid=false to restore the integration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — The find-then-create sequence is non-atomic, allowing concurrent first-delivery webhooks to create duplicate credentials or fail one delivery after external state has advanced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a find-then-create pattern in app-credential.ts lines 57-85: first findFirst() is called to check if credential exists, then either update() or create() is called based on the result. This is indeed a race condition - if two concurrent webhook requests arrive for the same userId/appId combination, both could pass the findFirst check (returning null), and both would then attempt to create(), potentially resulting in duplicate credentials or a unique constraint violation. This is a real concurrency bug in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:56 — Decrypted credential JSON is never validated against the selected app's credential schema, so an authenticated malformed delivery is acknowledged and corrupts the live credential.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, the code decrypts the keys at line 53-55 using `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` but never validates that the decrypted JSON conforms to the expected credential schema for the specific app. The code then directly uses these keys in prisma.credential.update() or prisma.credential.create() without any schema validation. This means malformed but successfully decrypted JSON could corrupt the credential data in the database. The finding correctly identifies that there's no validation against the app's credential schema before storing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — The configured sync endpoint returns a Fetch Response, but this adapter reads the Axios-only `data` property so synced Google token refreshes are discarded.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts (lines 83-97), the code calls `refreshOAuthTokens()` which wraps the refresh function. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true, `refreshOAuthTokens` (in refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 6-14) returns a fetch Response directly. However, the GoogleCalendarService code then accesses `res?.data` (line 91) which is an Axios-style property access. A fetch Response object doesn't have a `data` property - it has methods like `json()`. So when credential sync is enabled, `token` would be undefined, and the refreshed tokens would be lost. This is a real bug in the integration between the new sync mechanism and the existing Google Calendar code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — The shared sync helper returns a Fetch Response while this caller treats it as HubSpot's camelCase token object, persisting undefined tokens and an invalid expiry.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the original token refresh call with refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either a fetch Response object (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true) or the result of the refreshFunction. The original code expected hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken() to return a HubspotToken object directly. When credential sharing is enabled, the code receives a fetch Response instead of the expected HubspotToken structure, but then tries to access properties like hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken and hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn (lines 191-193 in the original code pattern). This type mismatch would cause undefined values to be persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — The advertised access-token-and-expiry response contract does not actually accept or preserve an arbitrary expiry field because the computed Zod key becomes a literal property and unknown fields are stripped.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 5-10, the schema definition uses `[z.string().toString()]` as computed property keys. This doesn't create dynamic property matching - `z.string().toString()` returns '[object Object]' or similar string representation, not a dynamic key matcher. Zod doesn't support arbitrary key matching this way. The schema won't properly validate responses with varying expiry field names (like 'expires_in', 'expiry_date', etc.) as intended. The code comment says 'Assume that any property with a number is the expiry' but the implementation doesn't achieve this. This is a real bug where the schema validation won't work as documented/intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — With no configured webhook secret, an absent header compares as `undefined` and permits an unauthenticated credential write.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts lines 22-27, the code checks if APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true before proceeding. APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is defined in packages/lib/constants.ts as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. So if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set, APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED would be falsy and the endpoint returns 403. However, if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set but empty string (''), the check `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` would compare undefined (missing header) to empty string, which are not equal, so it would return 403. The finding claims that with no configured webhook secret, an absent header permits unauthenticated access, but this is incorrect because APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED would be falsy if CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set, blocking access at line 18-20.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Credential-sync returns a Fetch `Response`, but it is treated as a `HubspotToken`, causing undefined token fields to be persisted.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the token refresh call with `refreshOAuthTokens()`. The `refreshOAuthTokens` function (in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns a `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is true (it returns `await fetch(...)`), but returns the result of `refreshFunction()` otherwise. In the HubSpot case, `refreshFunction` returns a `HubspotToken` object from `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken()`. When credential sync is enabled, the code assigns the fetch Response to `hubspotRefreshToken` which is typed as `HubspotToken`, but it's actually a Response object. The subsequent code tries to access `.accessToken`, `.refreshToken`, `.expiresIn` properties which don't exist on a Response object, leading to undefined values being persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — The `any` callback and inferred union return erase whether callers receive a Fetch `Response` or an SDK-specific token object, allowing every adapter to assume an incompatible shape without type checking.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that refreshOAuthTokens in the diff (lines 3-21 of refreshOAuthTokens.ts) uses `refreshFunction: () => any` and returns either the result of refreshFunction() or a fetch Response, creating a union type that erases type safety. Looking at the diff, different callers pass different types: Google passes `fetchTokens.res`, HubSpot passes the result of `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken()`, and others pass fetch Response objects. The function returns these heterogeneous types without type checking. This is a legitimate architectural/type-safety concern introduced by the new abstraction, though it's not a bug per se since the code may work at runtime - it's a design issue that could lead to future bugs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:13 — Accepting `any` and `ZodTypeAny` and returning the whole safe-parse wrapper leaks validation mechanics while discarding the schema's inferred token type, which has already led callers to consume and persist the result inconsistently.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real design issue in the new parseRefreshTokenResponse function. Looking at the diff, the function accepts `any` for response and `z.ZodTypeAny` for schema (lines 12-13), and returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper rather than the validated data. This is visible in how callers use it inconsistently - in GoogleCalendarService.ts line 96, the result is assigned directly to `key` without accessing `.data`, while in Office365CalendarService.ts line 261, it's used with `.success && tokenResponse.data`. The function also mutates the result by adding a default refresh_token (lines 24-26). This is a legitimate architectural concern about type safety and API design in newly added code, though it's not a bug since the code can still function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15 — Token validation is coupled to global environment state instead of the response source, so local refreshes that fall back because a credential has no userId are still parsed under the sync-endpoint contract.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts lines 14-17, the function checks `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` to decide which schema to use. However, in refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 4-6, the same condition is checked but also requires `userId` to be truthy before calling the sync endpoint. If userId is null/falsy, refreshOAuthTokens falls back to calling the local refreshFunction, but parseRefreshTokenResponse still uses the minimumTokenResponseSchema (because it only checks the env vars, not whether the sync endpoint was actually used). This means local refresh responses could be validated against the wrong schema.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:40 — Resolving the app through both the database and `appStoreMetadata` creates two registries that must remain synchronized for the webhook to accept an integration.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the webhook handler at lines 36-48 first queries the database for the app by slug, then looks up appStoreMetadata using that same slug. This creates a dependency where both registries must have the app for the webhook to work. Looking at the diff, line 36-40 shows `prisma.app.findUnique({where: {slug: reqBody.appSlug}})` and line 46 shows `appStoreMetadata[app.slug as keyof typeof appStoreMetadata]`. This is a valid architectural concern - if an app exists in the database but not in appStoreMetadata (or vice versa), the webhook will fail. This is a legitimate design/architecture concern introduced by this new code, though not strictly a bug since both registries should be synchronized in normal operation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — The credential-sync fetch has no abort timeout, so an unavailable sync service can indefinitely block expired-token booking requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — Sync mode returns a Fetch Response but this path reads a Gaxios `.data` field, so every Google token refresh through the sync endpoint falls back to the expired token.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, the code wraps the refresh token call with refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either the fetch Response directly when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true, or returns the result of refreshFunction() otherwise. In the Google case, refreshFunction returns `fetchTokens.res` which is a Gaxios response with a `.data` property. However, when sync mode is enabled, a raw fetch Response is returned instead. The code at line 94 then does `const token = res?.data` - this works for Gaxios responses but a fetch Response doesn't have a `.data` property (it has methods like .json()). This means in sync mode, `token` would be undefined, causing the token refresh to fail silently and fall back to expired credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — Persisting the SafeParse result rather than its `.data` stores `{success,data}` as the Google credential and makes subsequent authentications fail validation.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 100 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then line 101-103 shows `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns the result of `schema.safeParse(response)` which is an object with `{success, data, error}` structure, not the actual parsed data. The code should be using `key.data` instead of `key` when updating the credential. This would store the wrong structure and break subsequent authentication attempts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — Sync mode returns a Fetch Response where HubSpot expects a parsed token object, so refresh writes/uses undefined token fields and leaves the client unauthenticated.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens function wraps the original token refresh call. The code then uses hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken, hubspotRefreshToken.refreshToken, etc. directly without parsing the Response. This means in sync mode, these properties would be undefined, causing authentication failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 — The sync response is documented to omit refresh tokens, but the parser injects `"refresh_token"` and this merge overwrites the usable Office 365 refresh token.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:93 — Saving the access-token-only sync response replaces the Teams credential and drops its refresh token, preventing recovery when the next token expires.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens function is called at line 60-78. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, refreshOAuthTokens returns the response from the sync endpoint (lines 6-14 in refreshOAuthTokens.ts), which only contains access_token and expiry. When the credential is updated in the database (implied by the flow), the original refresh_token would be lost. This is a real bug affecting token persistence for Teams credentials when credential sync is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — An unset CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET makes an absent header compare equal to undefined and bypasses webhook authentication

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at lines 23-26 of app-credential.ts, the code checks `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || 'calcom-webhook-secret'] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set (undefined), and the header is also not present in the request (undefined), then `undefined !== undefined` evaluates to `false`, meaning the check passes and authentication is bypassed. This is a real security vulnerability where an unset environment variable allows unauthenticated access to the webhook endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — No sync-enabled refresh test exercises a real Fetch Response, so the code reads the nonexistent res.data and silently keeps the expired token.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, the refreshOAuthTokens function wraps the original refresh call and returns either a custom fetch Response (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED) or the result of the refresh function.
